followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and the models' self-reported task preferences.

On capability, this is a structured listing task — produce 80 names split into two categories. That falls under Extraction & Retrieval, where Lapwing scores 81.6 vs Willet's 79.2. That gap is just over the 2.0-point "treat as a tie" threshold, so it counts as a mild real edge for Lapwing, though honestly it's marginal.

The more decisive factor was preferences. Willet self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work, but this isn't really open-ended — it has clear completion criteria (40 + 40 names), which is actually the kind of task Willet rates *highly*. So the preference argument doesn't strongly push toward Willet either way here.

Given that, I leaned on the small Extraction & Retrieval edge for Lapwing and the fact that nothing about the task disadvantages it. The documentation also notes preferences are dissociated from output quality, so my routing was about fit and small benchmark margins, not expected answer quality — which would be very close on either model.

In short: it was a close call, decided by Lapwing's slight retrieval-eval advantage on a well-specified listing task.
